document.title: Document Naming Conventions
document.scope: Historical 2012 source edition. Not a current rule set, official schema, or identity authority.
document.text_policy: Text is based on the supplied normalized conversion of the PDF, not original PDF bytes or line layout. Source paragraph boundary whitespace is trimmed. Internal source paragraph text is retained; paragraph boundaries within cells become newlines. Examples are exact substrings of those paragraphs. Source typos, inconsistent codes, repeated examples, and retained committee directory entries are not repaired.
document.coverage: All 45 retained body sections, all 40 retained source tables and their 320 rows, retained body paragraphs/list text, nine footnotes, code definitions, and the full historical committee directory are available as JSON. The historical member directory (source section 46, pages 30–40) and its duplicated source-text anchors are intentionally omitted. PDF page geometry, graphic pixels, table-of-contents leaders, cover layout and repeated page furniture are also outside this semantic catalog.
document.provenance_policy: Source IDs are stable opaque anchors. Each anchor resolves to source text inside source_nodes in this same JSON document. No external markup or document is needed.

omitted_content.reason: The historical roster is intentionally excluded. Bioguide identifier fields and naming-rule examples remain; no bundled roster or identity resolution is required.

measureTypeLower.description: Selected output spelling: lowercase, matching numbered-measure samples. Not a source-wide rule about case.

legislativeStage.description: Stage codes printed in the 2012 appendix; no current completeness or type/chamber compatibility claim.

committeeCode.description: Filename code syntax only. Two-character committee examples and four-character subcommittee examples are both represented. The appendix labels its four-character codes as folder codes; no folder-to-filename alias is inferred.

bioguideId.description: Syntax only. Does not require membership in the 112th-Congress directory.

filenameToken.description: Selected safe single filename value: no whitespace, path separators or control characters. No transliteration, case conversion or punctuation cleanup is performed. Resource and portability bounds are implementation constraints. A trailing -U<digits> is reserved; no Unicode normalization is performed.

witnessId.description: Supply the prepared last-name-plus-first-initial token or a member Bioguide ID. The schema cannot establish that this token matches a real person or that a name was prepared correctly. Resource and portability bounds are implementation constraints. A trailing -U<digits> is reserved; no Unicode normalization is performed.

date8.description: YYYYMMDD lexical check. Calendar validity is checked by the included adapter, not this regular expression.

fiscalYear.description: Printed two- or four-digit fiscal year. No century is inferred for a two-digit year.

sequenceId.description: Digits preserved exactly. No fixed padding width is inferred from a sample.

amendmentId.description: Literal local amendment identifier, including letters and underscores. Enbloc and terminal revision suffixes are separate fields.

extension.description: Deliberately bounded output convention: PDF and XML extensions observed in this source. Not a claim that the source prohibits every other extension.

revision.description: Omit for the initial posting. The adapter appends -U followed by this number before the extension.

meetingOccurrence.description: Omit for the first meeting that day; subsequent occurrences become a -2, -3, ... suffix.

committee_print_link_url.description: Absolute HTTP(S) URL. The runtime applies deterministic structural checks, including prepared ASCII URI spelling and percent escapes; format is an annotation for external consumers. No URL is fetched and no publisher is authenticated.

hearing_transcript_link_url.description: Absolute HTTP(S) URL. The runtime applies deterministic structural checks, including prepared ASCII URI spelling and percent escapes; format is an annotation for external consumers. No URL is fetched and no publisher is authenticated.

hearingPublicationType.description: GPO hearing publication type printed in the package identifier.

hearingPublicationSuffix.description: Printed publication suffix retained verbatim, alongside separately extracted explicit part, volume, addendum and errata tokens.

publicationExtension.description: Observed government publication filename extensions; no content format validation.

publicationPartId.description: Printed part, volume, addendum or errata identifier. Empty means an unnumbered marker is present; omission means absent.

reportDocumentType.description: A congressional report. Conference status is not established by the filename.

reportPublicationType.description: Printed House, Senate, or Senate executive report code.

versionSuffix.description: Literal suffix after the legislative stage; retains occurrence, annotation and local descriptive text.

stageOccurrence.description: Printed occurrence following a version code; distinct from a document revision.

annotation.description: Text inside a printed parenthetical annotation.

appropriationType.description: Explicit suppl or CR marker within the AP/FY description; no annual status is inferred from its absence.

voteIdentifier.description: Literal vote identifier, range or label; no range expansion or vote count is inferred.

amendmentSubject.description: Selected safe single filename value: no whitespace, path separators or control characters. No transliteration, case conversion or punctuation cleanup is performed. references.description: Literal references found within known filename fields. Offsets are zero-based character positions [start,end) in sourceField. Related mentions never replace primary metadata, establish document relationships, or supply a missing source slot.

measureType.description: Selected output spelling: lowercase, matching numbered-measure samples. Not a source-wide rule about case.

year.description: Printed two- or four-digit fiscal year. No century is inferred for a two-digit year.

observedCongress.description: Three-digit Congress slot in observed incomplete layouts; fixes the boundary before an adjacent untyped numeric token.

untypedNumberToken.description: Printed numeric slot with no measure type. Leading zeros and zero placeholders survive; no bill identity is inferred.

observedDraftStage.description: Literal House pre-introduction marker in observed drafts without a measure-type slot; not added to the GovInfo version vocabulary.

draftDescription.description: Selected safe single filename value: no whitespace, path separators or control characters. No transliteration, case conversion or punctuation cleanup is performed. Resource and portability bounds are implementation constraints. A trailing -U<digits> is reserved; no Unicode normalization is performed.

incompleteAppropriationRouting.description: Observed incomplete AP routing: optional literal prefix, optional FC/SC/ORH, then AP description. Complete measure-type/stage layouts are excluded. Unknown prefix text is retained without assigning a measure or person.

untypedLegislativeStage.description: Observed legislative stages: the version vocabulary plus House PIH. PIH remains a House marker, not a GovInfo version.

optionalMeasureToken.description: Explicit measure-type slot, or the empty string when absent. An absent type is not inferred.

numberPlaceholder.description: Literal placeholder or empty number slot; not a zero, bill number, or missing-value substitute.

namedDraftLabel.description: Observed printed label. No acronym expansion or document-content assertion.

draftIdentifier.description: Printed local draft identifier, including placeholders and leading zeros.

introducedDraftStage.description: Explicit IH/PIH suffix in descriptive legislative filenames. Restriction avoids stripping arbitrary short version-looking endings from words.

draftDescriptor.description: Literal descriptive text ending before an explicit IH/PIH stage. No person-name splitting or expansion.

numberedSubject.description: Retained numbered subject. Only an explicit known measure type permits deriving a measure identity.

measureList.description: One or more adjacent explicit measure references. Each occurrence is extracted independently; no primary measure is selected.

measureListPrefix.description: Literal optional SA prefix before the reference list. No legislative-version label is assigned.

measureListSuffix.description: Literal suffix after the legislative stage; retains occurrence, annotation and local descriptive text.

numberedDraftDescriptor.description: Literal descriptive text ending before an explicit IH/PIH stage. No person-name splitting or expansion.

unnumberedVersionSuffix.description: Literal suffix after the legislative stage; retains occurrence, annotation and local descriptive text.

amendmentSuffix.description: Literal suffix after HAmdt, not an amendment number. The guide identifies empty, 2 and 3 as first, second and third degree; other spellings remain uninterpreted.

amendmentDegree.description: Interchamber amendment degree identified by HAmdt/SAmdt, HAmdt2/SAmdt2, or HAmdt3/SAmdt3. Not an amendment sequence number.

statements.text: An alternate name for this version is Senate Amendment Ordered to be Printed. This version contains an amendment that has been ordered to be printed.

An alternate name for this version is House Sponsors or Cosponsors Added or Withdrawn. This version is used to add or delete cosponsor names. When used, it most often shows numerous cosponsors being added.
An alternate name for this version is Agreed to by House. This version is a simple or concurrent resolution as agreed to in the House of Representatives.
An alternate name for this version is Agreed to by Senate. This version is a simple or concurrent resolution as agreed to in the Senate.

An alternate name for this version is House Committee Discharged from Further Consideration. This version is a bill or resolution as it was when the committee to which the bill or resolution has been referred has been discharged from its consideration to make it available for floor consideration.

An alternate name for this version is Senate Committee Discharged from Further Consideration. This version is a bill or resolution as it was when the committee to which the bill or resolution has been referred has been discharged from its consideration to make it available for floor consideration.
An alternate name for this version is Considered and Passed by House. This version is a bill or joint resolution as considered and passed.
An alternate name for this version is Considered and Passed by Senate. This version is a bill or joint resolution as considered and passed.

An alternate name for this version is Engrossed Amendment as Agreed to by House. This version is the official copy of a bill or joint resolution as passed, including the text as amended by floor action and certified by the Clerk of the House before it is sent to the Senate. Often this is the engrossment of an amendment in the nature of a substitute, an amendment which replaces the entire text of a measure. It strikes out everything after the enacting or resolving clause and inserts a version which may be somewhat, substantially, or entirely different.

An alternate name for this version is Engrossed Amendment as Agreed to by Senate. This version is the official copy of the amendment to a bill or joint resolution as passed, including the text as amended by floor action and certified by the Secretary of the Senate before it is sent to the House. Often this is the engrossment of an amendment in the nature of a substitute, an amendment which replaces the entire text of a measure. It strikes out everything after the enacting or resolving clause and inserts a version which may be somewhat, substantially, or entirely different.

An alternate name for this version is Engrossed as Agreed to or Passed by House. This version is the official copy of the bill or joint resolution as passed, including the text as amended by floor action and certified by the Clerk of the House before it is sent to the Senate.

statements.text: This version is the official copy of the bill or joint resolution as passed and certified by the Clerk of the House before it is sent to the Senate. See H. J. RES. 280 from the 101st Congress for an example of this bill version.

An alternate name for this version is Enrolled as Agreed to or Passed by Both House and Senate. This version is the final official copy of the bill or joint resolution which both the House and the Senate have passed in identical form. After it is certified by the chief officer of the house in which it originated (the Clerk of the House or the Secretary of the Senate), then signed by the House Speaker and the Senate President Pro Tempore, the measure is sent to the President for signature.

An alternate name for this version is Engrossed as Agreed to or Passed by Senate. This version is the official copy of the bill or joint resolution as passed, including the text as amended by floor action and certified by the Secretary of the Senate before it is sent to the House.

This version was ordered to be printed by the Senate. For example, in the 105th Congress S. 1173 was considered at length by the Senate, returned to the Senate calendar, ordered to be printed. Then its text was inserted into its companion House bill which was passed by the Senate.

This version is a bill or resolution as it was when an action previously taken on it was undone or invalidated. For example in the 102nd Congress for H.R. 2321 the Senate action discharging the Energy Committee and amending and passing the bill was vitiated by unanimous consent. The bill was amended, reported, and passed anew.
This version is a bill or resolution as placed on one of the five House calendars. It is eligible for floor consideration, but a place on a calendar does not guarantee consideration.
This version is a bill or resolution as placed on one of the two Senate calendars. It is eligible for floor consideration, but a place on a calendar does not guarantee consideration.

Any bill from the House or Senate may be issued as a public print. If a bill is issued as a Public Print more copies will be printed than are printed for an engrossed version. Public prints also number the amendments made by the last chamber to pass it. Public Prints are typically published by the Senate to show Senate amendments to House bills. They typically contain the text of a House bill, indicating portions struck, plus Senate amendments in italics. They are routinely ordered for appropriations bills, but the Senate occasionally by unanimous consent orders public prints of other significant bills.
This version is a public print of a bill as passed. Generally, appropriation bills receive a PP designation while non-appropriation bills receive a PAP designation. See also Public Print.

pwah.label: Ordered to be Printed with House Amendment

statements.text: This version shows Senate amendments to a House bill. It is similar to a Public Print from the Senate, except that it does not include portions struck, only the Senate amendment in the nature of a substitute in italics. See S. 1059 from the 106th Congress for an example of this bill version on a Senate bill.
This version was referred with amendments to the House.
This version was referred with amendments to the Senate.

It may have been discharged from the committee to which it was originally referred then referred to a different committee, referred to an additional committee sequentially, or reported by the original committee then referred to an additional committee. See S. 1016 for an example of this bill version on a Senate bill.

It may have been discharged from the committee to which it was originally referred then referred to a different committee, referred to an additional committee sequentially, or reported by the original committee then referred to an additional committee. See H.R. 1502 from the 105th Congress for an example of this bill version on a House bill.

An alternate name for this bill version is Received in House from Senate. This version is a bill or resolution as passed or agreed to in the Senate which has been sent to and received in the House. See the 105th Congress for an example of this bill version.

An alternate name for this bill version is Received in Senate from House. This version is a bill or resolution as it was passed or agreed to in the House which has been sent to and received in the Senate.

This version has been re-enrolled.

This version is a bill or resolution as referred or re-referred to committee with instructions to take some action on it. Often in the Senate the instructions require the committee to report the measure forth with specified amendments.

text-00002.text: The House Rules for the 112th Congress call for greater transparency and accessibility to legislative documents.

text-00003.text: Specifically, two provisions were added to the rules by House Resolution 5:

text-00004.text: • Clause 3 of Rule XXIX provides that a measure or matter will have been considered as having been publicly ‘‘available’’ within the meaning of the rules if it was publicly available in electronic form at a location designated by the Committee on House Administration.

text-00005.text: • Clause 4(d)(1)(E) of Rule X directs the Committee on House Administration to establish and maintain standards for documents made available in electronic form by the House and its committees.

text-00006.text: The intention of these two provisions is to ensure that Members and the public have easy access to bills, resolutions, and amendments considered in committee and by the House. According to Chairman Dreier’s statements before the House, “The standard for electronic documents is intended to evolve over time. While the standard may initially include more static formats such as a searchable PDF, the intention is to eventually transition to more flexible structured data formats, such as XML, as the tools become available to ease the creation and ensure the integrity of House documents. With respect to availability, the provision is intended to place electronic distribution on par with traditional printing; rather than entirely replace it. Finally, the rule contemplates a singular location that will direct Members and the public to the text of measures to be considered by the House and its committees.”2

text-00007.text: The Speaker and House Leadership have directed the Clerk to create a centralized repository to provide access to documents that will be considered in committee and by the House. For 2011, the Committee on Rules is providing access to legislative text being considered by the House at http://rules.house.gov/billsthisweek.aspx?NewsID=337, and each committee is posting documents under consideration by the committee on their own websites. In 2012, the Office of the Clerk will maintain the site, http://docs.house.gov which will provide access to legislative text being considered by the House, and in 2013, the site will provide access to legislative text being considered by House committees.

text-00008.text: Additionally, the Committee on House Administration, as directed by House rules3, has established standards4 for posting House and committee documents and data electronically. As part of the standards, the Office of the Clerk has been directed to, “…publish and maintain naming standards for each document [required to be posted online as outlined in the standards]”. These standards will facilitate automated searching and uploading of such documents. Files will be posted using permanent URL links. These links will facilitate outside and committee usage of these files. In addition, permanent URL links will allow archived committee web sites to maintain functionality5.” This document describes the naming standards for electronic files for congressional documents covered under the aforementioned standards adopted by the Committee on House Administration on December 16, 2011.

text-00009.text: The goals in the naming conventions include:

text-00010.text: • Reduce duplicate document names in the committee repository;

text-00011.text: • Enable search and search engine capabilities;

text-00012.text: • Allow the document’s name to be self-identifying.

text-00013.text: Where possible, the naming standards follow existing naming conventions used by the Government Printing Office’s Federal Digital System (FDSys).

section-02.text: Linking to documents on GPO or THOMAS

text-00015.text: If a document has already been published and posted on GPO’s FDSys System or the LOC’s THOMAS system, it is acceptable and encouraged to link to these locations.

text-00017.text: Where it is necessary to have a member identifier in the file name, the Member’s Biographical ID number or Bioguide ID should be used. The current Members and their Bioguide IDs are listed in the appendix. For former Members, see http://bioguide.congress.gov.

text-00018.text: The benefits of using the Biographical ID number include having a unique identifier within and across Congresses, the Bioguide ID number is already in use by organizations in and outside of the Legislative Branch, and it avoids any duplicate document names due to duplicate or similar Member names.

text-00020.text: The conventions in this document will be updated when it is deemed necessary to add additional document types, add additional clarification to the naming conventions, or other circumstances.

text-00021.text: Starting with version 1.2 of this document, changes and addition will be noted in an appropriate footnote.

text-00023.text: If your committee would like to provide feedback on the naming conventions and their use, contact the Committee on House Administration.

policies: All patterns in this catalog are active. Implementation interpretations are documented on each pattern; no runtime profile selection or per-record acknowledgment is required.

Canonical output spelling is specified per template and field enum. Lookups are case-folded; parsing accepts ASCII case variants of fixed tokens and code fields and renders their canonical spelling. Free text retains its spelling. No automatic spelling correction, identifier padding, or name transliteration.

The terminal -U<positive integer> suffix is reserved for revision. Free tokens ending -U<digits> are rejected, including U0. Revision and meeting counters cannot have leading zeros; sequence and amendment identifiers preserve leading zeros.

Permitted extensions are defined per naming kind by its field enum; publication kinds also accept htm and html. These are implementation constraints, not claims that the guide prohibits other formats.
End users supply only JSON; a filename ending .xml does not entail reading or producing XML content.

Resource bounds are implementation decisions: 255 UTF-8 bytes per validated filename, 160 characters per free token, 32 per sequence identifier, signed-32-bit maximum positive counters; prepared tokens exclude whitespace, controls, slashes and Windows-forbidden punctuation. Literal extraction instead accepts source basenames up to 16384 UTF-8 bytes; remainder refinement raises a structured limit error above 128 steps or 262144 retained field characters.
Date fields are lexical YYYYMMDD in JSON Schema; the runtime also checks the Gregorian calendar and Monday week starts.

Committee folder codes are never silently converted to filename tokens. The retained committee directory is historical lookup data, not a filename acceptance allowlist. No member directory is bundled; Bioguide identifiers receive syntax validation only, not identity or membership checks.

Multiple matching patterns are returned together. A match indicates only this implementation’s grammar, not normative document classification, person identity, file existence, uniqueness, publication authority, or legal compliance.
Exact source-example membership is independent of runtime validation. A malformed source example remains retrievable without bypassing validation.
Templates and the catalog are trusted, versioned local configuration, not arbitrary untrusted grammar input. They are compiled without eval and without network resolution.

Reference URLs use prepared ASCII URI spelling, valid percent escapes, an HTTP(S) scheme, a nonempty parsed host, a valid port when present, and no credentials. This structural URL check is implemented without optional format plugins; it does not promise full RFC conformance or publisher identity.
